profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Corporate Research Insights team and the Market Strategy team at a financial services firm preparing a client-facing briefing note based on an internal research paper about Taylor-rule-based monetary policy analysis in the US and UK from 1990 to 2020. The immediate context is that the economist has finished the core empirical analysis and the strategy team needs the right outputs packaged for a cross-asset weekly client deck. The agenda is to align on what will be handed off this week: which version of the results table goes into the shared deck, what 'stability over the shock period' will refer to in charts and commentary, what the augmented Taylor-rule asset-price variable should cover, and what counts as a 'robustness check' for the strategy note appendix. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, timing, and shared artifacts so the deck and appendix can be assembled without another meeting.

members.name: Aisha Patel
members.expertise: Monetary policy modeling, econometrics, cross-country macro comparisons
members.background: Aisha has a master's degree in economics, previously worked in a central bank research unit, and now produces empirical research for institutional clients at an asset management firm.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve methodological consistency with the paper draft already shared with her director, avoid reopening modeling choices, and keep the handoff lightweight by sending near-final research tables rather than making presentation-specific custom outputs.
hidden_assumptions: The 'shock period' naturally means the 2008-2009 global financial crisis window because that is the structural break period used in her baseline stability checks.
The 'augmented' Taylor rule uses broad equity-market volatility as the asset-price channel, operationalized through monthly realized volatility aligned to her macro sample.
A 'robustness pack' means econometric diagnostics sufficient for a research appendix: residual normality, Newey-West corrected estimates, and GMM outputs from the final model specification.
The 'comparison table' refers to the cleaned coefficient summary table from her latest working file, where significance markers and country panels are already standardized for internal review.

members.name: Daniel Reeves
members.expertise: Client briefing production, cross-team coordination, financial market storytelling
members.background: Daniel came from an equity strategy publishing team and now coordinates how research outputs are translated into recurring client products across rates, equities, and multi-asset strategy.
members.private_state: He wants the note to plug cleanly into the weekly deck template, minimize back-and-forth with design, and ensure the story ties monetary policy to market behavior in a way clients expect, without asking the research team for too many revisions.
hidden_assumptions: The 'shock period' naturally means the 2020 pandemic dislocation because clients currently interpret 'shock' as the COVID-era market regime.

The 'augmented' Taylor rule should speak to equity prices in a client-facing sense, so the relevant asset-price field is a broad stock index level or return series rather than volatility unless stated otherwise.

A 'robustness pack' means the set of outputs needed for publication support: one main specification, one backup specification, and concise notes showing the result survives reasonable presentation-level scrutiny.
The 'comparison table' refers to the table already circulated in last week's deck-prep folder, which he assumes is the current approved version for downstream use.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to include commentary on 'stability over the shock period.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the 2008-2009 global financial crisis break window used in her coefficient stability checks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the 2020 COVID market shock window, which he expects because it is most salient for clients.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see 'shock period' as an obvious shorthand in macro-finance work, and because the project already spans 1990-2020, neither feels a need to restate which shock episode is intended.

misalignment_points.topic: Which asset-price measure is being added
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss 'adding asset price' in the augmented Taylor rule for the client note.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the asset-price term already constructed in her models: monthly equity-market volatility for each country.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of a stock-market series clients recognize directly, such as the S&P 500 and FTSE 100 index level or return measure.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The seed topic and client audience make 'asset price' sound self-explanatory, and both participants know the study connects monetary policy to markets, so the phrase feels sufficiently specific even though they map it to different variables.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having a 'robustness check appendix' ready for the deck support materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this appendix will include only formal econometric diagnostics from the final specification: normality, Newey-West, and GMM results.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes it also includes a simplified alternative model version and a short explanation of whether the headline comparison still holds under a more client-digestible setup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat 'robustness checks' as standard support material, but one thinks in terms of technical test outputs while the other thinks in terms of publication-ready backup evidence, and that difference is rarely spelled out in coordination meetings.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'comparison table' is the handoff artifact
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using 'the comparison table' in the shared folder.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this means the latest coefficient summary table in her econometrics workspace, updated after correcting UK output-gap standard errors.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this means the table in last week's deck-prep folder that design has already formatted and tagged for publication.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There really is a known comparison table in circulation, and both believe there is only one salient version; the meeting focuses on handoffs, so neither thinks to confirm file lineage or revision date.
